gaps: No verified cost estimate for children with a parent in prison (219,000 a year).
No cost-effectiveness study for brain injury screening or linkworker support in justice settings.
No UK cost-of-illness estimate for FASD, and no verified UK return for children's speech and language therapy.
EIF's late intervention estimate has not been updated since 2016.
Most youth violence effect sizes come from outside the UK; UK trials of MST, FFT and FNP were null or not cost-effective.
Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland are thin outside alcohol pricing and the CPIT trials.
Few sources report QALYs; most report cash returns, so health and cash values cannot be combined without assumptions.

pocket.text: £1,177 per family, repaid 2.8 to 6.1 times across education, health, social care and justice over 25 years. No single commissioner sees the whole return.
Judged at birth the incentives look poor value (£150,000 per QALY). Over a lifetime, with the child's health counted, they save money.
Early years spend repaid through the NHS, SEND, social care and, mainly, higher tax receipts decades later.
NHS England pays £659 per referral; courts and prisons save £933, chiefly through fewer custodial remands and sentences.
Local authorities pay and recover £4.50 per £1 in four years. The larger gain, fewer children entering care, falls on the next generation.
Schools deliver the programme; the return appears only when parents' reduced absence from work is counted.
